    Bug 2050249 - comm_taskgraph: import release_level from mozilla-taskgraph instead of gecko_taskgraph r=thunderbird-build-system-reviewers,maxe,coreycb
    
    release_level was moved from gecko_taskgraph to mozilla-taskgraph (released in 4.2.0). See https://github.com/mozilla-releng/mozilla-taskgraph/pull/220.
    
    The new signature is `release_level(release_branches, params)`, where release_branches comes
    from the graph config's release_branches mapping rather than a hardcoded dict in gecko_transform's attributes.py.
    
    This bug repoints comm_taskgraph's release_level consumers at mozilla-taskgraph and supplies the mapping from config:
    - Add a release-branches: mapping to `comm/taskcluster/config.yml`.
    - Switch the transform consumers `(hardened_signing, release_flatpak_repackage, update_verify_config, l10n, l10n_pre, push_langpacks)` to import release_level from `mozilla_taskgraph.util.attributes` and pass `graph_config["release-branches"]`.
    - Update `comm_taskgraph/util/taskgraph_attributes.py` (the RUN_ON_PROJECT_ALIASES "release" alias) to call the new release_level with a module-level mapping, since that path runs in the target-task filter chain and has no graph_config.
    
    This depends on [2050201](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2050201) and [2050242](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2050242) before this can land.
    
    Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D308639
